idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After deploying v2.3.1, checkout-api began failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of 18%. Its staging candidate, v2.3.1-rc, had also been unhealthy. checkout-api was rolled back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback the service reports healthy with an error rate of 0.2%. Next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure and work out why the release went to production even though the staging candidate was unhealthy.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged the on-call engineer.

**Rollback**
- The latest deploy, v2.3.1, was failing health checks in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an 18% error rate.
- v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. The other releases since then (v2.3.1 and its staging candidate v2.3.1-rc) were both unhealthy.
- After the rollback, all three regions are on v2.3.0 and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
- No approval was needed, because v2.3.0 has been healthy in production before.

**Incident INC-0001**
- It says v2.3.1 failed health checks, describes the rollback and the recovery, and lists two follow-ups: find the root cause, and work out why v2.3.1 went to production when its staging candidate was unhealthy.
- My first attempt to open it timed out. The incident list was still empty afterwards, so I retried with the same idempotency key (which prevents a duplicate). Exactly one incident exists.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
